title: Columnwise quasi-isomorphisms induce first-quadrant total quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let K and L be first-quadrant double complexes [def-sp-double-complex-total], and let f:K→L be a double-complex morphism. Suppose for every n the map of resolution columns K.flip.X n→L.flip.X n induced by f is a quasi-isomorphism, that is, it induces isomorphisms on every homology object. Then the canonical total map Tot(f):Tot(K)→Tot(L) is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 12.25.4, finite-diagonal argument, applied to column cones

proof.text: For a fixed homology degree n put N=n+1. Restrict each vertical complex to the finite shape with indices 0,...,N and extend by zero. The shape embedding has predecessor-closed image, hence its stupid truncation has a canonical projection. Map this functor and projection along the horizontal complex. The resulting square for f commutes by πStupidTrunc_f_naturality. Every term above row N is zero.

At a retained vertical degree q≤N, the flipped projection is an isomorphism of horizontal complexes, since every component is an isomorphism. Its naturality square identifies the truncated horizontal map with the original one by an isomorphism of arrows. At q>N both horizontal complexes are zero. Therefore every horizontal map of the truncated bicomplex is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the finite-row comparison lemma.

The total projection is an isomorphism in degree m≤N: every summand has p+q=m and thus q≤N, so its component is invertible; use GradedObject.isIso_mapMap_apply. In particular it is invertible on the three terms computing degree-n homology, including prev(0)=0. Thus it is a quasi-isomorphism at n by quasiIsoAt_iff' and ShortComplex.quasiIso_of_isIso. Totalize the naturality square and apply two-out-of-three at n to transfer the finite-row comparison to the original total map. Repeat for every n, using quasiIso_iff.

proof_origin.place: Finite row filtration of the total complex; finite diagonal locality, implemented by E1
